description: C1 golden fixture — the PBO gate must feed DECIMAL returns into compute_crra_eu_objective, not RAW PERCENT. The autotuner objective stores cscv_date_returns; pre-fix it stores raw percent (a -1% day as -1.0), which the decimal-contract utility floors to WEALTH_ARG_FLOOR (W=max(0.001,1+r) collapses to 0.001 -> U=-999). Post-fix the store divides by RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION so a -1% day is -0.01 (W=0.99, U~=-0.0101). No producer-computed value is hardcoded: every expectation is derived from the raw input via the named RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION constant or asserted as a shape/finiteness property.
citation: Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014, DOI 10.21314/JCF.2014.005; validation/overfitting.md C1; GATE2-PLAN A1.
provenance: Hand-authored RED scenario inputs (raw percent guard-alpha series). Expected decimal values are DERIVED from the raw inputs by dividing by RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION (=100.0). No compute_crra_eu_objective output is pinned as a literal; the floor-collapse assertions are inequalities (finite, > -1.0) not exact floats.

constants._note_constants: These mirror autotuner.RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION and math_engine.WEALTH_ARG_FLOOR. Tests read the live module constants and only use these for fixture self-consistency checks.

sub_one_percent_day_raw_vs_decimal.description: A single -1% day. Raw percent stores it as -1.0 (floors W to 0.001 -> U=-999 collapse). Decimal stores it as -0.01 (W=0.99, no floor).
sub_one_percent_day_raw_vs_decimal._assertion_kind: the test derives expected decimal = raw / RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION at runtime; it does not hardcode -0.01

mixed_guard_alpha_series_raw_percent.description: A multi-day raw-percent guard-alpha series including a sub--1% day. The decimal-unit utility over this series must be FINITE and > -1.0 (no WEALTH_ARG_FLOOR collapse). The raw-percent utility floors and collapses to a large-negative dominating value.
mixed_guard_alpha_series_raw_percent._assertion_kind: shape/bound — decimal mean(U) in (-1.0, +inf) finite; raw mean(U) <= some large-negative collapse. No exact float pinned.

pbo_veto_preserved_under_correct_units.description: A config set whose PBO is genuinely low (IS-best generalizes OOS) must still PASS the PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD gate (pbo <= 0.5) AFTER the unit fix. Inputs are already DECIMAL (what the consumer compute_pbo contracts on); this pins that the caller-side unit fix does not flip a correct veto decision. configs and dates are synthetic; the assertion is on the gate decision (pass), derived from the computed PBO vs the live PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD constant.
pbo_veto_preserved_under_correct_units._assertion_kind: decision — pbo <= live PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD (veto does NOT fire). Config 0 dominates IS and OOS; the IS-best generalizes. No exact PBO float pinned.
